subject: zoology_2
question_text: Why are the arteries more elastic than the veins?

verification.note: Sourced from 'My Baby Bullet-Q — Senior Inter Zoology' (Star-Q Pass Track Series, Sri Publishers, 2022), book p.48, VSAQ 64. The printed exam years are the book's claim, reproduced here as appearances. Zoology-II holds only ONE source book in the corpus, so the two-book union check is structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is our reading of the question and is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Text revision (examiner audit, 2026-09-05): the mistakes note no longer calls 'arteries carry oxygenated blood' true without qualification, because the pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood, and the insider note no longer states what the board deducts.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: High pressure in arteries
steps.why: Blood leaves the heart in spurts, so an artery has to stretch with each beat and spring back between them.
common_mistakes: Saying arteries carry oxygenated blood. Most do, but the pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood, and in either case this is not the reason arteries are elastic.
steps.margin_note: Name the pressure. That is the marked reason.
lines: Arteries are more elastic because they must
cope with the high pressure of blood pumped
The pressure in the major arteries is
higher than in the minor arteries.

steps.label: Low pressure in veins
steps.why: By the time blood reaches a vein the pressure has been used up in the capillaries, so no springy wall is needed.
common_mistakes: Writing that veins have no walls. They have walls with little elasticity.
Forgetting to compare. The question asks for a comparison.
steps.memory_tip: Low pressure, thin walls, little elasticity.

lines.text: Veins have low pressure and less elastic walls

insider_note: This is a 'why' question with two halves. The complete answer gives the reason for the artery and then the matching statement for the vein.
